fragments.text: Target edition: 16 October 2026. Uptime is a complete website uptime and API monitoring product for a US small-business site or application operator replacing Pingdom (SolarWinds), UptimeRobot, Better Stack Uptime or Site24x7, with the monitoring-as-code and transaction depth buyers seek from Checkly, OpenStatus and Hyperping. Prices/budgets are USD, phone defaults are US numbers, and schedules/reports support US time zones and daylight saving.

The product discovers, operates and maintains trustworthy monitoring of the actual customer outcome: HTTP/API, every named protocol below, job heartbeats, multi-region and private checks, browser transactions, expiring assets, actionable alerts and reporting. Oncall owns full responder coordination and Lamp owns customer-facing status communication; their integrations are part of Uptime's monitoring job. No gap in implementation reduces this destination.

This is a target contract, not a release verdict. Every named clause states the buyer behavior and its acceptance journey. The final table distinguishes done, partial and missing at current code; a cited local test does not establish hosted placement, live migration, provider receipt or accessibility certification.
Existing clause IDs and the owner-accepted 13 October archive policy and 16 October three-second readiness budget are preserved.
This documentation round changes no homepage, interface or runtime behavior.
| Category | Website uptime and API monitoring |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Pingdom (SolarWinds), UptimeRobot, Better Stack Uptime, Site24x7 (and the monitoring-as-code challengers Checkly, OpenStatus and Hyperping) |
| First buyer | A US small-business site or application operator |

**HTTP-001 — Signed HTTP monitoring.** Public hosted HTTP(S) and keyword checks run in the Cloudflare Worker; private checks use the separately scoped Node runner. They retain the exact immutable assertion bundle and bounded transport evidence, and require authenticated claims and signed results; the control plane must reject contradictory completion. Hosted Worker checks leave through Cloudflare's shared egress and have no dedicated source address; published allowlistable probe addresses and probe identification are PROBE-002's. See [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority) and [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Create an HTTP(S) and keyword monitor through the owner API, run scheduled hosted and signed runner work against a controlled HTTPS service, fail its status/text, recover it and inspect the immutable assertions and transport evidence.

**EVIDENCE-001 — Immutable scheduled evidence.** Definitions, scheduled slots and every retry attempt retain revision, policy, fixed selected probes, runner identity, timings, status, assertions and error category; retries never erase failures, and observation/state/outbox commit atomically. See [Evidence and state](#evidence-and-state) and [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Through signed claim/result routes submit failure, retry, late and duplicate attempts, restart, and read history; each attempt and its revision remains identifiable and observation/state/outbox either all commit or none do.

**STATE-001 — Fixed coverage and incident hysteresis.** Missing or expired passing coverage is Unknown, partial failure stays visible, independent-vantage agreement and scheduled confirmation determine Failing, and complete fresh scheduled passing evidence plus recovery threshold is required for recovery; manual checks and maintenance never rewrite observations or scheduled policy. See [Evidence and state](#evidence-and-state). **Acceptance evidence:** Run two assigned network vantages through partial, missing, stale, failing and recovering slots; inspect Unknown/Degraded/Failing and thresholds. A manual pass, absent probe or maintenance expiry cannot fabricate recovery.
**AUTHORITY-001 — Server-side scoped authority.**
Every private document, read, mutation and export requires server-side operator or

scoped runner authority, missing configuration fails closed, browser mutations enforce configured origin, and expired/foreign attempts cannot alter current evidence, and duplicate attempt identities cannot overwrite it; a signature identifies a key holder rather than proving truthful observation. See [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Open private documents and call native/framework APIs while signed out, revoked, cross-origin or using a foreign/expired runner signature; require refusal with no product writes, then succeed with the authorized session or scoped runner.

**NETWORK-001 — Pinned bounded destination execution.** Every public DNS answer and redirect hop is validated fail closed; private-runner numeric sockets preserve Host and TLS identity, hosted checks use Cloudflare’s public Internet fetch transport, unsafe/mixed addresses and HTTPS downgrade are rejected, cross-origin redirects strip request authority, and synthetic grants and protected origin-bound local credential files retain their separate custody limits. The PROBE-002 identification header follows these credential rules and is stripped on cross-origin redirects. See [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Exercise real controlled HTTP/TLS endpoints with mixed DNS, rebinding, hostname mismatch, redirects, downgrade, forbidden addresses, credentials and execution bounds; inspect requests and prove rejected destinations receive no connection or authority.

**HEARTBEAT-001 — Revision-scoped receipt evaluation.** Hashed owner-issued tokens and, in the header form, increasing sequences protect server-time receipts, ingress cannot advance health, and scheduled signed completion must match its exact installation-local claim snapshot; stale, future, paused, foreign-revision or imported receipts cannot establish Healthy. These rules bind every receipt form of the buyer-facing job heartbeat in HEARTBEAT-002. See [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Issue and rotate a heartbeat token through the owner door, send increasing receipts, miss one, and evaluate scheduled signed snapshots; replay, old tokens, imported or foreign-revision receipts cannot change current health.

**ARCHIVE-001 — Inactive validated restore.** Bounded versioned archives require integrity and semantic validation before transactional restore into empty product data, preserve historical evidence, erasure receipts and the permanent anonymized action audit, create paused current revisions, interrupt leases and quarantine alerts; installation-local sessions, keys, grants, request credential values, heartbeat authority, contact, webhook and Slack URLs, and signing keys are excluded; destination definitions and retained notification histories are portable, and imported evidence cannot establish current health or replay events. The source erasure journal fences copies made before a later erasure when that journal accompanies the restore. A local CLI receiving checkout must run setup first to establish its owner and settings.
The owner accepted this installation-authority and endpoint-credential archive policy on 2026-10-13; it is an intentional replacement, not BASE-DATA-001 equivalence.

See [Portability and retention](#portability-and-retention) and [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Export a populated installation including TCP, DNS, TLS and domain monitors, establish a different receiving owner, import into empty product data, then export/read history and repeat the restore. Each protocol’s settings and immutable revisions/slots survive; definitions are paused, leases interrupted, delivery quarantined, secrets/authority absent, history retained and later erasure journals enforced; corrupt/nonempty imports write nothing.

**IMPORT-001 — Reviewed definition files and inactive imports.** A versioned definition file (2 MiB, 500 monitors, UTF-8 JSON, editor fields only, no request secrets or installation authority) or saved UptimeRobot v3 monitor pages are previewed without writes as create, unchanged, change, refused or unsupported per entry with a plan digest, validated by the editor's own validation; apply refuses a digest that no longer matches and otherwise resumes the reviewed plan in bounded transactional batches as new paused monitors or new revisions that keep enabled, maintenance and runner assignments; nothing in a file enables a monitor, issues a heartbeat token, schedules a notification or touches a destination.
Whole-plan atomicity is not established by the current door; whether batch atomicity meets the intended guarantee remains unresolved under this partial clause.

Undo pauses what it created and restores what it changed while their revisions are unchanged, reports the rest and never removes history. Legacy definition batches travel in archives as restored history without authority; import-door custody stays installation-local. Through this definition-file door a log export is recognized and counted only. Storing it as labeled source history for reports is HISTORY-001's migration import, and no imported history ever becomes evidence.
Unmeasured: no real UptimeRobot export and no hosted run.

See [Definition files and imports](#definition-files-and-imports). **Acceptance evidence:** Preview, apply, export and undo definition JSON and saved UptimeRobot pages through the owner routes and CLI. Malformed/hostile/secret-bearing inputs and stale digests write nothing; creations stay paused, changes keep operational state, unsupported fields are named and history is never made current evidence.
**RETENTION-001 — Explicit storage custody.**
Product and observation metadata and
legacy development sign-in records
have no automatic age/count deletion; operator erasure removes captures for the associated operator, and local reset clears the installation.
Expired sessions, authentication/public rate-limit state and

short-lived login-attempt counters are cleaned up. Expired or confirmed alert-drill links lose their capability material while drill history stays; retired destination secrets are scrubbed only after owner rotation/deletion and in-flight sends finish; a proven-unsent integration-attempt reservation can be removed while its delivery history remains.
Other expired operational records, including
discovery jobs,
change status and remain stored unless an owner erases the associated entity or resets the installation.

Raw target response bodies and probe-request secrets are not retained in observations; the only target content kept is EVIDENCE-002's bounded, redacted, access-controlled failure snapshot, stored apart from observations under owner-set retention, carried in archives and erased with its monitor or on owner request. Webhook and Slack endpoint URLs and signing keys remain installation-local, available email addresses travel as destination definitions, and retention changes must never silently improve the fixed denominator or historical health. See [Portability and retention](#portability-and-retention). **Acceptance evidence:** Judge custody and every declared cleanup class at current supported bounds. Populate product, authentication, rate-limit, drill, credential and attempt records; run expiry, maintenance and restart through runtime doors and compare surviving identities. Only declared transient data/secret material disappears; no cleanup improves uptime or removes retained product history.

**ERASURE-001 — Operator-directed entity erasure.** An owner can erase a monitor with its evidence and dependent notification/heartbeat records, a destination with its credential copies, or an operator while another active owner remains. Monitor erasure requires typing the current monitor name. Each completed erasure returns a receipt with entity kind, per-table counts and completion time, and returns it only after the transaction containing the erasure, audit entry and portability fence succeeds. Requests based on stale monitor or destination state cannot re-create erased rows. The last active owner cannot be erased: local installations use `rer reset --yes`, while hosted installations require replacement by redeployment. Uptime has no R2 attachment feature; import-door uploads, plan snapshots and archive bytes are D1 custody covered by the erasure rule below. Already downloaded archives, messages already sent to external recipients and requests already in progress remain outside local erasure. See [Erasure and audit](#erasure-and-audit). **Acceptance evidence:** Erase each supported entity through the owner API, including stale concurrent requests and the original owner with a successor. Inspect the atomic per-table receipt, audit and journal; the last owner is protected and an old archive with the later journal cannot resurrect erased records.
**AUDIT-001 — Durable anonymized audit.** Destructive actions, automated notification attempts and operator authentication-mail sends record
actor or feature, time,
action, subject kind and an opaque subject reference.
Audit history is portable
and survives erasure of the subject;
erasing an operator anonymizes its prior actor references.

The audit contains no monitor names, target URLs, email addresses or destination URLs. See [Erasure and audit](#erasure-and-audit) and [Portability and retention](#portability-and-retention). **Acceptance evidence:** Perform destructive actions, notification attempts and authentication-mail attempts through public doors, erase an actor and round-trip an archive; inspect durable opaque subjects and anonymized actors without planted names, addresses, URLs or secrets.

**PRESENCE-001 — Contact separate from health.** Only accepted scoped claims and signed results refresh server-time contact, the 120-second freshness threshold never proves process liveness or target health, and restart, unavailable reads and archive omission preserve that distinction. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance evidence:** Read Never seen, make accepted idle claims/results, age contact, reject foreign requests and restart. Reads and health checks do not refresh contact; unavailable reads and restore cannot imply runner or target health.

**INTERFACE-001 — Honest durable operator feedback.** Textual state/freshness/reasons, immutable history, labels, keyboard controls and responsive layout expose persisted evidence; failed reads show Unknown, action errors survive polling, busy reconciliation excludes controls and editing rejects assertion overrides. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance evidence:** Use the real owner console at 1440 and 390 with healthy, stale, failing and unavailable monitors; edit assertions, force read/action errors and polling, navigate by keyboard and inspect focus, text state, overflow, accessibility tree and axe results.

**NOTIFY-001 — Authorized installation-wide destinations.** An owner may configure email, signed JSON webhook, or Slack incoming webhook destinations for all monitors in one installation; only scheduled incident transitions generate automatic notifications, and a test send cannot change monitor evidence or incident state. The hosted Worker submits email through the configured Base mail adapter and sends webhooks and Slack without a private runner; a private runner can also claim notification work. Webhook destinations also take WEBHOOK-001's configurable method, content type, custom headers and payload template. Destination credentials are installation-local and are not restored from archives. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery) and [Network and credentials](#network-and-credentials). **Acceptance evidence:** Create/rotate/disable email, Slack and signed webhook destinations, cause scheduled failure/recovery and a test send through actual Worker/runner delivery doors; inspect one job per enabled destination, credentials, exact signing, escaping and unchanged health for tests.

**DELIVERY-001 — Bounded notification acknowledgment.** Each event and destination without receiver-side deduplication (email, Slack incoming webhooks and the other channels DELIVERY-002 names), every test send and every drill gets one automatic send attempt. A RER relay 429 with Retry-After confirms non-acceptance and queues another submission after that delay. For those sends HTTP 500, connection loss, timeout, and unknown outcomes remain uncertain and are not automatically sent again; deduplicating destinations retry and every route can fall back to another contact under DELIVERY-002. Accepted means the configured provider or endpoint acknowledged the request; it does not mean a person received, read, or acted on it. See [Contact, interface and delivery](#contact-interface-and-delivery). **Acceptance evidence:** At authorized provider edges return accepted, proven-unaccepted relay 429, HTTP 500, timeout and connection loss; restart during claims. Only the proven-unaccepted case requeues automatically; uncertain started sends never replay and acceptance remains distinct from receipt.

**PUBLIC-001 — Public landing and documentation.** At the app origin, `/` is the unauthenticated Lobby, `/docs` is public documentation, `/setup` is first-run setup, and the private operator console and editor are `/app` and `/app/monitor`; private documents require an owner session. The separate marketing site serves `https://run-uptime.com/` and `https://run-uptime.com/run`. The app Lobby at `/` and the marketing landing at the run-site `/` are distinct surfaces. **Acceptance evidence:** Open app-origin Lobby, docs and setup signed out, then sign in for /app and /app/monitor; separately read the marketing site and /run. Their routes remain distinct and private documents reject unsigned access.

**BOUNDARY-001 — Monitoring ownership and honest delivery claims.** Uptime owns checks, evidence, routing, repeat reminders and monitoring reports. It feeds full paging and responder coordination to [Oncall](https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall), PagerDuty or Splunk On-Call, and public incidents, branded pages and subscriber updates to [Lamp](https://github.com/just-every/run-lamp) or Atlassian Statuspage. Teams, Discord, Telegram, SMS, voice and push are supported target channels under the clauses below. One network label is one vantage; provider acknowledgment never proves human receipt or response. Geographic placement, browser execution and accessibility require their own measured evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure an alert and a sibling handoff, inspect acknowledged/received/responded as separate facts and simulate lost probes/providers; no duplicate network labels, acknowledgment or missing evidence becomes a delivery or availability guarantee.

**DRILL-001 — Recipient-reported alert drills.** An owner can run an alert drill on one destination: the existing test event with drill wording, sent once through the same path with no automatic resend, plus a one-time confirmation link (random capability, stored only as a bound hash, single use, 24-hour expiry, one drill and one destination). Opening the link shows a page; only a same-origin POST confirms, and unknown, used, expired and foreign links answer 404 alike. The console keeps Submitted, Acknowledged (or Uncertain/Failed with its code) and Recipient confirmed as separate lines, and does not measure whether anyone acted. A confirmed drill is a report by the recipient that one message reached a person at one time. It is never evidence of monitoring, a delivery guarantee or a human response, and it changes no monitor evidence, state or incident. Proof belongs to the destination's current credential: a new address or URL or a rotated secret makes it Never proven, and drill history stays with the installation, so a restored destination is Never proven. See [Alert drills](#alert-drills). **Acceptance evidence:** Drill email, Slack and signed webhook through the actual delivery runtime: GET/HEAD never confirm, same-origin POST confirms once, expired/replayed/foreign links refuse, 500 stays uncertain, rotation resets proof and archives/logs contain no capability or endpoint secret.

**STARTUP-001 — Required configuration diagnostics.** A shared configuration table validates required and conditional bindings for the Worker, scheduled entry point, local app, preview, setup, deployment and private runner before each begins work. Missing or malformed required values stop the entry point and name the variable without printing its value; a Worker configuration failure returns 503, including at `/health`. Hosted mode requires the selected Base mail provider and its sender configuration. See [Configuration diagnostics](#configuration-diagnostics). **Acceptance evidence:** Start each runtime entry point with required and conditional bindings missing/malformed; diagnostics name bindings without values and health returns 503. Restore settings and recover; exercise D1/ASSETS faults inside the owner-approved three-second readiness response budget.

**PUBLIC-002 — Declared sessionless paths and rate limits.** Every sessionless route and emitted static path is declared in `seed.json` with its authentication rule and rate-limit class. D1 applies owner-tunable per-client limits in fixed 60-second windows and returns 429 with `Retry-After` after the class limit. A declaration does not bypass route-specific session, runner, heartbeat or development-key checks. Limit values are marked estimated and not load-tested. See [Public paths and rate limits](#public-paths-and-rate-limits) and [Integrity and authority](#integrity-and-authority). **Acceptance evidence:** Enumerate declared sessionless paths against emitted routes, exceed configured public limits, inspect Retry-After, and remove counter storage; each route retains its own authentication checks and admission fails closed.

**FLOW-001 — Supported isolated browser transactions.** Login, signup and checkout are supported monitored customer paths with explicit intended outcomes, immutable revisions, safe synthetic accounts and scheduled consensus. A constrained editor and isolated Playwright execution share the same evidence and authority rules. Every required outcome must pass; missing browser/credentials is Unknown. Per-run process/profile isolation, sanitized environment, network filtering, hard time/byte limits and credential-origin binding apply to all scripts. Human approval is required for effects beyond an explicitly authorized synthetic transaction. A changed-definition recovery is labeled and never presented as proof of the original outcome. Support qualification covers independently placed real-browser vantages and the complete login, signup and sandbox checkout outcomes. Reusable scripts and fixtures are required under FLOW-002, failure artifacts under FLOW-003, browser/device coverage under FLOW-004, and setup/teardown and effects grants under API-004; secret-bearing grants require ACCESS-003 second-factor step-up, and reports spanning migrated history require HISTORY-001 source segments. FLOW-001 is done only when its own acceptance and each of these dependent clauses are done. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure supported login, signup and sandbox checkout journeys, run independent real-browser vantages, break required outcomes and recover through signed results. Wrong credentials, missing elements, server errors, slow pages, private redirects/subresources, extra origins and absent browsers have distinct retained outcomes; weakened definitions cannot silently clear the original incident.

**NETWORK-002 — Explicit TLS trust exceptions for legacy targets.** For self-signed, private-CA or legacy targets, a monitor can pin a buyer-supplied CA certificate or a leaf-certificate SHA-256 fingerprint (the preferred option). It can instead set an explicit per-monitor "ignore certificate errors" option, which an owner enables after a warning. Either exception is labeled on the monitor and in its evidence, and each slot records the TLS error it bypassed. An exception never applies after a redirect to another origin, and request credentials (API-002) are never sent to an unverified certificate unless that monitor's owner has granted it separately. TLS-001 still reports the certificate truthfully, and NETWORK-001's full verification remains the default. UptimeRobot's "ignore SSL errors" setting and its Pingdom equivalent import onto this option and are named in the preview. **Acceptance evidence:** Against a controlled self-signed target, see the default check fail with a TLS error, then pass with a pinned fingerprint and with the ignore option. Rotate the certificate and see the pinned monitor fail. Follow a cross-origin redirect and see verification enforced. Inspect the labels and the bypassed-error evidence, and import an UptimeRobot monitor with "ignore SSL errors" set and see the option in the preview.
*Status:* done.

fragments.text: **ARCHIVE-002 — Whole-workspace archives at monitoring scale.** Whole-workspace export, OPS-001 backup and restore handle SCHEDULE-002's scale: 500 monitors on 30-second checks from 3 locations (about 4.3 million attempts a day) with at least 90 days of retained history. The archive streams in bounded chunks under a manifest with per-chunk digests rather than as one 2 MiB document. Restore keeps ARCHIVE-001's validation, inactive-restore and erasure-fencing semantics and resumes after interruption. Exports for a time range or a subset of monitors are available. Any remaining bound is shown in the console before export, and an export over that bound refuses with its counts; it never truncates.
Storage capacity and archive size at this monitoring scale remain unmeasured; current view/archive bounds are not storage-capacity measurements.

**Acceptance evidence:** Populate 500 monitors with 90 days of 30-second, three-location history, export it, interrupt and resume the export, and verify the manifest digests. Restore into an empty installation and compare every table's counts and ARCHIVE-001 transformations. A 120-monitor account exports in full, and a range or subset export matches its selection.

**MONITOR-001 — Owned monitor catalog and lifecycle.** An operator organizes monitors by project, environment, service, tags, owner and dependencies; bulk create/edit/pause/resume/clone/search/filter preserve revision and incident history. Every monitor names its intended customer outcome, schedule, locations, assertions, maintenance and alert policy. Pausing never erases downtime. Bulk add takes a pasted list of URLs (one per line) or an uploaded CSV of up to 500 rows. The CSV has a `url` column and optional `name`, `type`, `keyword`, `interval`, `tags` and `group` columns. Settings shared across the batch (type, interval, locations, alert route, tags) fill whatever the rows leave out. A preview without writes marks each row as create, duplicate of an existing monitor, or refused with its reason (an invalid URL, a forbidden destination under NETWORK-001 or a quota). It also shows COST-001's projected traffic and cost. Apply creates the accepted rows in one transaction, as one IMPORT-001-style undoable batch. The monitors start paused unless the owner chooses "enable after create" in the reviewed preview. **Acceptance evidence:** Create production/staging monitors in the console/API, bulk change a selected tag, clone one, pause/resume another and compare revision, ownership and incident history before/after. Paste 50 URLs, including a duplicate, an invalid URL and a private address, with a shared 60-second interval, two locations and a route. The preview marks 47 creates, 1 duplicate and 2 refusals with reasons. Apply with "enable after create" and see 47 monitors checking on their first slot. Undo the batch, and a CSV upload with per-row names and tags produces the same plan.
*Status:* partial.

fragments.text: **API-001 — Complete HTTP and API assertions.** HTTP(S) methods, safe redirects, custom headers/body, expected status sets/ranges, keyword presence and absence, response headers, latency, nested JSONPath and regular-expression assertions evaluate the exact saved bundle with bounded redacted diagnostics. A transport 200 cannot pass a failed business assertion. **Acceptance evidence:** Save checks through the editor/API against a controlled endpoint; independently break absent/present keywords, status range, response headers, JSON arrays/nested paths, regex and latency, then inspect the distinct failures and unchanged saved criteria.

**SLOW-001 — Slow-response alerts distinct from outages.** A monitor can set a slow threshold, separate from any API-001 latency assertion: a response time over N consecutive slots, or a percentile over a window, per location or across locations. Crossing it opens a Slow degradation event with its own route, contacts and notices under ROUTING-001/ROUTING-002, plus a slow-recovered notice. A Slow event is not an incident: it does not count as downtime in availability or SLA figures, and REPORT-001 reports it as slow time. A latency assertion stays a failure for buyers who want slowness to count as down. Pingdom `responsetime_threshold` and Site24x7 static greater-than response-time thresholds with consecutive poll-count rules map onto Slow during migration. Site24x7 AI, average/time-window and percentile strategies explicitly refuse conversion and require an owner-set local policy. Better Stack’s [public Uptime API monitor schema](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/create-a-new-monitor/) exposes `request_timeout`, a transport failure timeout, and no separate slow-threshold field. A Better Stack `request_timeout` maps only to the transport timeout, never to Slow; cutover asks the owner to set a slow threshold explicitly. Uptime retains the full consecutive/percentile, per-location/across-location Slow capability. **Acceptance evidence:** Set a 2,000 ms slow threshold over 3 slots on a controlled endpoint and slow it to 3,000 ms. A Slow notice reaches its route, no incident opens, uptime is unchanged and the report shows slow time. Recover and see the slow-recovered notice. A latency assertion on another monitor still fails that monitor as down.

**API-002 — Authenticated monitoring and secret lifecycle.** Basic, HTTP Digest and bearer, OAuth 2.0 acquisition/refresh, JWT signing and mTLS client certificates use owner-authorized secret references, least scope, expiry/rotation and exact origins. Test accounts and credentials remain under installation/runner custody; auth errors remain distinguishable from application failures and secrets never enter evidence or exports. **Acceptance evidence:** Use each authentication mode against an authorized endpoint, expire/rotate/revoke it and redirect cross-origin; show expected failure/recovery, refusal of foreign references and no planted secret in storage, logs, browser artifacts or archives.
*Status:* done.

fragments.text: **API-003 — Multi-step API transactions.** A scheduled backend transaction shares scoped authentication, variables and extracted response values across ordered requests, asserts each business outcome and records per-step timing. Setup, failure and cleanup remain visible; a later success cannot erase an earlier failed requirement. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a login/create/read/delete API journey through the supported configuration door, fail a middle assertion and expire shared auth, then inspect step history and cleanup without leaking extracted secrets.

**API-004 — Safe setup and teardown.** Browser and API journeys run bounded setup/teardown fixtures using synthetic accounts, Stripe test mode and buyer sandbox resources; cleanup runs after failure or cancellation and leaves durable actionable cleanup debt when it cannot complete. Live purchases, destructive writes or refunds require an exact time-limited grant and spend limit.
As built:

setup and cleanup steps make at most 3 attempts inside the wall time and a reserved cleanup share, and the count is retained per step; request steps are never replayed. A browser flow's optional setup and teardown fixtures use the API step vocabulary, engine, origin and network controls, and extracted values stay on the runner. A cancellation stops the journey, still runs cleanup and is recorded as cancelled (Unknown), never a pass; teardown never changes a browser verdict. A cleanup step that cannot complete (denied at the network edge, out of attempts, or missing a value the target reported creating) is a visible cleanup failure and leaves one retained cleanup debt naming the monitor, revision, slot, attempt, step, attempt count, last failure category and created time, with its open or resolved state and resolution note and time; it holds no extracted value, credential or response body, travels in archives and is removed by monitor erasure. Open debt is separate from monitor health: it never makes a failing target Healthy or a healthy one Failed. At 3 open debts for a monitor the next run refuses new setup and reads Unknown with the named reason; only the owner's explicit, idempotent and audited resolution closes debt, never a later passing run. A step is live when the owner marks its effect (`live-payment`, `refund`, `destructive-write`), it is a refund, anything it sends has a Stripe live-mode key shape, or its response says `livemode: true`; it is refused (runner category `grant`, nothing sent except for a live response) unless an active grant names the monitor and effect, with an expiry within 24 hours and an integer spend limit (a request spends its integer `amount`, at least 1), rechecked on every attempt. Grants are revisioned, audited and installation-local; the default is no grant. Stripe test mode and the buyer's sandbox resources need none. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a sandbox checkout with setup/teardown, cancel mid-flow and deny cleanup at the network edge; inspect bounded attempts, retained cleanup failure and explicit operator resolution without a live charge.

**TCP-001 — TCP service checks.** TCP monitors test a chosen host/port, handshake latency and optional bounded banner from selected locations with the same confirmation, evidence and alert policy as HTTP. Refused connections, timeout and probe failure remain distinct. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a TCP monitor through the console/API; open, close and blackhole an authorized port from two locations, then read evidence and trigger/recovery events.

**PING-001 — ICMP reachability and packet quality.** ICMP ping monitors retain bounded packet loss, round-trip latency and configured thresholds by location for IPv4/IPv6. ICMP blocked by policy is shown explicitly rather than inferred from HTTP success. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure a ping target, vary loss and latency, disable ICMP and stop a probe; inspect protocol-specific results and Unknown probe coverage.

**DNS-001 — DNS records and change detection.** Checks query selected recursive and authoritative resolvers for A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, SRV and CAA records, expected values, absence/change and response time. NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, propagation differences and monitor infrastructure faults are distinguishable; owner-approved expected changes suppress only their own condition. **Acceptance evidence:** Save DNS monitors via the owner door, change/remove an expected record and induce resolver disagreement/failure; inspect raw bounded record evidence, confirmed alerts, maintenance and recovery without treating a missing answer as success.

**TLS-001 — SSL certificate and chain monitoring.** TLS checks verify hostname/SNI, certificate chain/trust, validity, expiry and renewal on HTTPS or configured TLS ports from each location. Staged configurable expiry warnings name the certificate and accountable owner, track renewal and resolve only after a newly observed valid chain. **Acceptance evidence:** Monitor a controlled TLS service; present an expiring certificate, broken chain, wrong name and then renewed certificate, advance the clock and inspect deduplicated warnings, location evidence and renewal resolution.

**DOMAIN-001 — Domain registration expiry.** Domain monitors use RDAP and authorized registrar/WHOIS data, retain source/freshness, warn the owner before registration expiry and follow through until renewal is independently observed. Redacted, unavailable or conflicting registry data is Unknown; certificate renewal is not domain renewal. **Acceptance evidence:** Add a domain in the console, drive authorized registry-edge responses through approaching expiry, unavailable data, conflicting dates and renewal; inspect distinct warnings, source times and resolved follow-up.

**UDP-001 — UDP request and response checks.** Bounded UDP checks validate configured payload/response and timing on an authorized host/port with anti-abuse traffic limits and location consensus. No response is not treated as proof of an open port. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a UDP monitor, return matching/mismatching payloads, drop packets and remove probe authority; inspect timeout versus assertion versus runner failures and bounded outbound traffic.

**MAIL-001 — SMTP and mailbox protocol checks.** SMTP/STARTTLS, POP3/POP3S and IMAP/IMAPS checks verify connection, TLS, banner, authentication and optional synthetic send/receive transaction with a dedicated test mailbox. Message IDs, timing and cleanup are retained without mailbox content or passwords; a successful SMTP accept is distinct from mailbox receipt. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure each protocol via the owner door against authorized mail edges, break authentication/TLS and delay receipt; inspect per-step alerts, receiver confirmation and removal of synthetic messages.

**HEARTBEAT-002 — Cron and job heartbeat monitoring.** A buyer monitors a scheduled job by choosing either an expected period (30 seconds to 31 days) or a five-field cron expression with an IANA time zone (US zones offered first, daylight-saving gaps and repeats handled explicitly), plus a grace period (0 seconds to 24 hours).

A run is missed when no success ping arrives by its expected time plus grace: the scheduled evaluation due at that instant confirms Failing, never earlier, and a later success recovers it labeled as a late run.

The job can report its own failure without waiting for the window: a `/fail` or `/fail/<exit code>` ping schedules an immediate evaluation, so the incident opens within SCHEDULE-002's alert bound with the exit code and a bounded redacted output excerpt (request body up to 10 KiB, owner masks and EVIDENCE-002 secret patterns applied); a later success recovers it.

An optional `/start` ping measures run duration: a run exceeding the owner's maximum duration alerts as Running too long, a start with no finish is a missed run, and every completed run's duration appears in history and REPORT-001.

Receipts accept GET, HEAD and POST so curl, wget, PowerShell and HTTP-only schedulers work, either through a URL-capability form (rotatable, hashed at rest, rate-limited and labeled replay-unprotected, matching incumbent heartbeat URLs) or the sequence-protected header form; both keep HEARTBEAT-001's revision, ingress and import rules, and no ping by itself establishes Healthy.

The console and API generate copy-paste snippets for crontab, curl/wget, systemd timers, Kubernetes CronJob, GitHub Actions and Windows Task Scheduler that wrap a command so start, success and failure with exit code are all reported.
Heartbeat migration uses documented source settings through the MIGRATE clauses, with newly issued Uptime URLs.

[UptimeRobot](https://github.com/uptimerobot/ai/blob/main/skills/create-heartbeat-monitor/SKILL.md) `interval` and `gracePeriod` (seconds) map to Uptime period and grace; [Better Stack](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/create-a-hearbeat/) `period` and `grace` (seconds) map directly.
Source alert contacts, delays/repeats and escalation settings are reviewed under the migration and routing clauses, never treated as grace.

[Site24x7 heartbeats](https://www.site24x7.com/help/heartbeat/index.html) document no separate period/grace pair: their threshold profile sets late-ping Trouble and Down deadlines and an early-ping Trouble threshold.

MIGRATE-004 requires the owner to choose an explicit local period and grace whose sum preserves the selected missed-ping deadline, and names any Trouble/early-ping behavior requiring a separate policy rather than silently converting it.
[Pingdom’s documented check types](https://docs.pingdom.com/api/) contain no heartbeat, cron or push check: Pingdom has no heartbeat check; nothing to migrate.
These source limits do not reduce Uptime’s cron, IANA/DST, receipt, period or grace capabilities.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through the console and API configure `0 2 * * *` in America/New_York with 15-minute grace; skip one run and see the alert open at 02:15 local time and not before, including across a DST change.
Send `/fail/3` with output containing a planted token and see an immediate incident naming exit code 3 with the token masked, then recover with a success.
Send `/start`, then success after 40 minutes against a 30-minute maximum, and see Running too long plus the recorded duration.

Receive GET, HEAD and POST pings; run each generated snippet unmodified against a real shell or scheduler edge; rotate the URL and prove the old URL, a replayed header sequence and an imported receipt cannot establish Healthy.
For UptimeRobot, preview `interval: 3600` and `gracePeriod: 300`; for Better Stack, preview `period: 3600` and `grace: 300`.

Each becomes a paused 60-minute period plus 5-minute grace, discards source URL authority, and after owner activation with a new URL fails only at the 65-minute deadline and recovers on a late success.
Reconcile each source’s alert settings separately.

For Site24x7, review a 10-minute Trouble and 30-minute Down threshold plus an early-ping threshold; an owner-selected 25-minute period and 5-minute grace preserves the Down deadline, and the preview names Trouble and early-ping differences for explicit policy review.
No Pingdom heartbeat entry or invented field is requested.

fragments.text: **SCHEDULE-001 — Explicit cadence, retries and confirmation.** Each revision records interval, timeout, retry budget, freshness, failure/recovery slot thresholds, fixed selected probes and assignments. Scheduled work cannot count retries as independent slots, invent missed checks or let manual runs alter cadence. Outages shorter than the sampling interval may be missed; SCHEDULE-002 sets the interval floor, on-time rate and alert latency. **Acceptance evidence:** Save a cadence through the API/CLI, run retries, delay claims, edit the interval and make a manual pass; inspect due times, fixed coverage and incident thresholds through history.

**SCHEDULE-002 — Interval floor, on-time execution and alert latency.** Every protocol monitor (HTTP/API, keyword, TCP, ping, DNS, UDP, mail and heartbeat) can run every 30 seconds from each selected managed location, with 60 seconds as the default; TLS and domain expiry checks run at least hourly and browser transactions as often as every minute. A plan or budget that imposes a slower floor shows it before activation under COST-001. Cadence holds at scale: with 500 monitors at 30 seconds from three locations in one workspace, at least 99% of slots per location are claimed within 5 seconds of their due time and 99.9% within 15 seconds over any hour. Each location's on-time rate and lag distribution is visible in the console and METRICS-001, and a late or missed slot is recorded as such and counts as Unknown rather than being skipped silently. From the commit of the observation that confirms an incident to the first delivery attempt for every routed destination takes at most 10 seconds at p99, excluding and showing any ROUTING-002 delay. The editor shows each monitor's worst-case detection time for its saved settings (confirmation slots × interval + timeout + retry budget + the alert bound). Capacity or quota shortfall is visible and halts or labels work under COST-001; it never quietly stretches an interval. **Acceptance evidence:** Through the public API create 500 monitors at 30 seconds from three managed locations against controlled targets and run them for at least one hour; compute claim lag from stored slot records and compare it with the console and metrics figures. Fail a target and measure from the confirming observation's commit time to each destination's first attempt start. Remove one location's capacity and see late or missed slots reported and coverage turn Unknown; reach a quota and see named halted work rather than a longer interval; compare the editor's detection-time figure with the measured outage-to-alert time.

**PROBE-001 — US and global independent locations.** Buyers select managed US East, Central and West plus Europe and Asia-Pacific locations, see operator/network/region identity and IPv4/IPv6 coverage, and configure duration/location consensus. A lone network blip never fires a confirmed outage; independent target observations or an independently passing canary corroborate it. Probe health and regional partial failure remain visible; no label pretends to be physical independence. **Acceptance evidence:** Run an authorized public target from real US and global locations, break only one probe network and then the target, stop a region and recover. Inspect independent network evidence, Degraded/Unknown coverage and confirmed trigger/recovery.

**PROBE-002 — Published probe addresses and identification.** Every managed location sends checks from stable dedicated egress addresses. Uptime publishes each location's IPv4 and IPv6 list as plain-text and JSON files, as DNS A/AAAA records under a documented name per location plus one all-locations name, and through an unauthenticated machine-readable API that always returns the current list with a version and effective date; the console also shows the subset a buyer's own monitors use. Address additions and removals are announced at least 30 days ahead by email to owners, a changelog/RSS feed and a `pending` section of the API, and a new address carries checks only after that notice period; an emergency change is labeled as such with its reason. Every hosted request carries a documented User-Agent naming Uptime, its version, a probe documentation URL and an opaque monitor reference, plus an optional per-installation secret header buyers can match in Cloudflare, AWS WAF, Akamai or origin bot rules; the header follows NETWORK-001's credential rules and is stripped on cross-origin redirects. The current Cloudflare Worker vantage uses shared egress with no dedicated address: until it moves behind published egress the console labels it not allowlistable and offers a published location instead. Private runners (PRIVATE-001) report their own observed egress address. **Acceptance evidence:** From each managed location run a real check against an authorized target that logs source address, User-Agent and header; every observed source appears in that location's published file, DNS answer and API list, and no unpublished address appears. Allowlist only the published addresses at a controlled WAF and see every location pass. Stage an address change and verify the notice, pending entry and 30-day hold before the new address carries checks; redirect cross-origin and prove the secret header is not forwarded; inspect the Worker vantage's not-allowlistable label.

**PRIVATE-001 — Buyer-network private locations.** Scoped buyer-owned runners monitor allowlisted intranet/VPC services with outbound-only control-plane access, revocable identity, capacity/upgrade/health visibility and secret locality. Explicit per-runner private hostname/CIDR/port grants are separate from public probes; metadata and management endpoints remain blocked. Datadog private-location users can deploy equivalent Uptime runners beside existing agents without forwarding Datadog credentials or misrepresenting its probes as ours. **Acceptance evidence:** Enroll a runner in an authorized private network, grant one service, execute HTTP/TCP/browser checks, then revoke it. Unauthorized neighbors, metadata, redirected private addresses and public-runner use of the grant refuse without connecting.

**MAINT-001 — Planned and recurring maintenance.** One-time and recurring windows target monitors/groups with US time zones, daylight-saving handling, preview and audit. Buyers choose notification suppression or execution pause explicitly; reports show maintenance separately and retain denominator and underlying observations. Expiry re-evaluates actual evidence and cannot emit orphan recovery. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a New York recurring maintenance window across a DST transition and a one-time group window; fail a monitor during each, restart, end/cancel the window and inspect preserved results, suppression and reports.

**REPORT-001 — Latency, uptime and SLA reporting.** Per-monitor/service/location charts show response-time percentiles, availability, outage duration, incident timelines and SLA/SLO attainment for buyer-chosen periods and US time zones. Export CSV/JSON/PDF and schedule email/Slack reports to authorized recipients; the same figures are available through READAPI-001's authenticated API, computed by the same code, for the same period, time zone and denominator. Incident lists and SLA reports can be filtered and grouped by INCIDENT-001 root-cause category, with incident count and downtime per category. Unknown, partial, paused and maintenance time and denominator policy are visible. Incumbent history imported under HISTORY-001 appears as a labeled source segment with its own denominator, next to Uptime's own slots and a blended cross-cutover figure naming both sources; it cannot improve current health. SLOW-001 slow time is reported apart from downtime. **Acceptance evidence:** Cause known failures, gaps, slow responses, maintenance and revisions; compare custom-period charts and downloaded reports to immutable slots, schedule a report, fail delivery and inspect its durable outcome. A report spanning a HISTORY-001 cutover shows the source and Uptime segments with their own denominators. A report filtered by an INCIDENT-001 root-cause category lists exactly the incidents with that category. Each downloaded report's figures equal READAPI-001's for the same period.

**EVIDENCE-002 — Failure snapshot and incident report.** Every failing attempt keeps an incident-report snapshot: the request actually sent (method, final URL, redirect chain and header names, with values redacted unless the owner marks them safe), response status, response headers and timing phases, and a bounded excerpt of the returned body (the first 16 KiB as text, shown only as escaped text or in a sandboxed no-script preview), so an operator sees the Cloudflare 52x page, maintenance page or stack trace the probe received. Before storage the excerpt passes owner masks plus built-in secret patterns (authorization values, cookies, API keys, card numbers, and email addresses unless allowed), and planted request secrets never appear. For HTTP and keyword checks the buyer can enable a screenshot of the failing page, taken by an isolated browser under FLOW-001's network rules. Incident detail combines these with a plain-language cause (for example, HTTP 503 from 2 of 3 locations whose body reads Service Unavailable), per-location results, DIAG-001 diagnostics and the activity log. Snapshots are stored apart from observations under owner-set retention (default 90 days), readable only by roles with evidence access, carried in archives, exported with their incident and erased with their monitor or on owner request with a receipt. They never alter a verdict, and alerts carry only a cause line and an authenticated link to them. **Acceptance evidence:** Fail an HTTP monitor against a controlled endpoint returning a 503 HTML page containing a planted API key, cookie and email address; as owner open incident detail and see the request, status, headers, page excerpt and screenshot with planted values masked. Open it as an unauthorized role and signed out and be refused; export the incident and round-trip an archive; erase the monitor and confirm the snapshot and its copies are gone with a receipt; inspect the alert for only the cause line and link.

**DIAG-001 — Connection and network diagnostics.** A confirmed timeout, connection refusal or reset, DNS failure or TLS failure automatically collects bounded traceroute/MTR, DNS, TCP and TLS phase timings from authorized probe locations, retains hop loss/latency, compares healthy regions and attaches the result to the EVIDENCE-002 incident report. Redaction and traffic caps apply; blocked diagnostics are explicitly unavailable and never alter the monitor verdict. **Acceptance evidence:** Trigger a controlled route/connect timeout and a refused connection, open diagnostics from incident detail and compare two locations with one ICMP-blocked path; inspect bounded artifacts, visible unavailable reason and unchanged incident.

**PERF-001 — Page speed and real-user performance.** Synthetic page-speed checks retain DNS/connect/TLS/TTFB, resource waterfall and Core Web Vitals budgets. An optional consent-aware browser beacon measures real-user availability/performance by route, device and region with sampling, privacy exclusions and bot filtering; RUM and synthetic denominators remain distinct. Buyers can find a slow mobile checkout despite a healthy health endpoint. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure a page-speed monitor and consented beacon on a controlled site, throttle mobile assets and produce a browser error; inspect waterfall, budget alert, privacy/sampling settings and separate RUM versus synthetic reports.

**DEPENDENCY-001 — External dependency checks.** Read-only discovery proposes third-party status components or public status endpoints as separate monitors with source attribution and reviewed assertions. Statuspage-compatible sources retain the overall-status proposal and offer bounded component proposals keyed by component ID, unticked by default. Adopted monitors retain the provider name as `service`, a `dependency` tag and an `outcome` line identifying the status as the provider's own claim. That claim is contextual evidence, never proof that the buyer application is up or down. A failed provider component is an ordinary separate monitor with its own state and ordinary scheduled incident policy; it never changes any application monitor's state, revisions, evidence, routes or incident thresholds. DEPENDENCY-002 inherits these attribution and separation rules and may replace the ordinary incident default with dependency notices that open no Uptime incident; correlation belongs to FOLLOWUP-001. The owner reviews and changes the component before adoption by selecting another proposal, or after adoption by editing the monitor as an ordinary immutable revision. A component’s `group` retains its reviewed name; switching components updates the name, `group` and component-ID assertion together. A renamed or removed component, or a status source that stops answering, is missing/Unknown evidence, never Healthy. **Acceptance evidence:** Discover a linked provider status page through the real runner, review/adopt its overall and one component proposal through the owner monitor door, then switch the component through an ordinary revision. Fail the selected component with scheduled signed-runner evidence and inspect the separate provider monitor's failure and named source while the application monitor's state, revisions and evidence remain unchanged; remove the component and inspect Unknown/missing evidence.

**DEPENDENCY-002 — Third-party service catalog.** An owner can add a named third-party provider directly from a searchable catalog, without running discovery. The catalog covers at least the providers US small businesses commonly depend on: AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, Cloudflare, Stripe, PayPal, Square, Shopify, GitHub, Vercel, Netlify, Twilio, SendGrid, Mailgun, Slack, Zoom, Atlassian, OpenAI, Anthropic, Okta, Auth0, DigitalOcean and Fastly. Each entry names the provider's official status source (a Statuspage-compatible JSON API, RSS/Atom feed or status page) and its components and regions. The owner can follow the whole provider or chosen components, such as Stripe API or AWS us-east-1 EC2. A followed service becomes a dependency monitor inheriting DEPENDENCY-001's attribution, contextual-evidence and separation rules; this clause replaces its ordinary separate-monitor incident default with dependency notices that open no Uptime incident. The provider's stated status is attributed contextual evidence, is never proof that the buyer's application is up or down, and never changes an application monitor's state. Provider incidents and recoveries notify through the owner's chosen ROUTING-001 route as dependency notices, not as Uptime incidents. They appear beside correlated application incidents under FOLLOWUP-001, and AGENT-002 can cite them. A dependency the owner links to a monitor, service or group (MONITOR-001) shows as linked and qualifies for grouped acknowledgment. An unlinked provider incident that overlaps in time shows only as contextual coincidence and never groups acknowledgment. Following an entry first checks its status source live; a failing source is marked needs review. An owner can add a provider not in the catalog by giving its status page URL, which goes through DEPENDENCY-001's reviewed proposal. Catalog entries are versioned and reviewed when a provider moves its status source. A source that stops answering makes that dependency Unknown, never operational. UptimeRobot, Better Stack and Site24x7 third-party service monitors map onto catalog entries during migration. **Acceptance evidence:** Search the catalog for Stripe and add it with only the API component followed, then add AWS us-east-1. At an authorized status-source edge, report a Stripe API incident: a dependency notice reaches the chosen route, no Uptime incident opens, and the application monitor's state is unchanged. Fail the application at the same time and see the correlated dependency on its incident. Make the status source unreachable and see the dependency turn Unknown. Recover the provider and see the recovery notice. Import an UptimeRobot account that follows Stripe and AWS and see both mapped onto catalog entries. Overlap an unlinked provider incident and see it labelled coincident, outside the group. Import a Better Stack and a Site24x7 account with third-party monitors and see them mapped, or the clause cites the public API showing no such field and the import refuses conversion.

**FLOW-002 — Reusable Playwright monitoring as code.** Buyers import and version real Playwright scripts, test suites and fixtures for login, signup and checkout alongside API checks, with dependency locks, selected secrets, setup/teardown and safe effects grants. Each run is isolated outside ordinary Worker requests; scripts cannot bypass destination or resource controls. Editor and code revisions expose the same required outcomes. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a real Playwright suite via CLI/GitHub Actions, preview and deploy it, then break a fixture, assertion and forbidden network call; scheduled runs preserve intended outcomes, isolation and reviewable revision history.

**FLOW-003 — Useful and safe browser failure artifacts.** Failed steps retain redacted screenshots, Playwright traces, video replay, console errors, network/timing waterfalls and step durations tied to the immutable run. Owner-defined masks, no secret-bearing headers/bodies and bounded retention/export/access prevent synthetic credentials or personal data leaking into artifacts. Artifact-generation failure is visible and cannot hide the check failure. **Acceptance evidence:** Break sandbox checkout, inspect screenshot/video/trace/waterfall through authenticated incident detail, deny artifact storage and try an unauthorized download. Planted secrets/masked fields never appear; retained artifact failures and erasure are visible.

**FLOW-004 — Cross-browser and mobile transactions.** A buyer selects Chromium, Firefox or WebKit and desktop/mobile viewport/device profiles per journey; reports and consensus preserve that browser/device dimension. Missing browser capacity stays Unknown. Native iOS/Android app testing is a separate device-testing integration; mobile web paths are Uptime checks. **Acceptance evidence:** Deploy the same checkout to all three browsers and a 390-pixel mobile profile, introduce a mobile-only failure and remove one browser; inspect per-profile failures and Unknown capacity without averaging them into success.

**ROUTING-001 — Monitor, service and team alert routing.** Route confirmed alerts by monitor/group, environment, severity, region, incident origin, team and US business/quiet hours; select multiple contacts with explicit inheritance, preview and test. Destination secrets stay installation-local and routing changes are auditable. A paused or disabled contact cannot silently count as covered. Per-contact delay and repeat are ROUTING-002's; retry and fallback contacts are DELIVERY-002's. The route's quiet-hour policy applies to every contact on the route, fallback contacts included. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure two teams and production/staging routes through the UI/API; trigger each class inside/outside quiet hours, rotate a destination and inspect selected/excluded recipients and drill outcomes.

**ROUTING-002 — Per-contact alert delay and repeat.** Each monitor, group or route sets, per contact, notify after X minutes down (0 minutes to 24 hours), repeat every Y minutes while down (off, or 1 minute to 24 hours, with an optional maximum count) and whether that contact receives recovery notices. A delayed contact is notified only if the same incident is still open when its delay elapses; a recovery inside the delay sends that contact nothing, including no recovery notice. Repeats are FOLLOWUP-001 reminder events with the incident's stable identity, stop on recovery or under the selected acknowledgment policy and never replay an uncertain send. Delays and repeats count from confirmation time, survive restart, appear in the route preview (for example, Slack now, SMS at +10 minutes, repeat every 30 minutes) and map from UptimeRobot's per-contact threshold and recurrence and Pingdom's notify-after and repeat settings. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure Slack at 0 minutes and SMS at +10 minutes with a 30-minute repeat; confirm an outage and see Slack at confirmation, SMS only at +10 minutes and a repeat at +40. In a second outage recover at +5 minutes and see no SMS and no SMS recovery notice; restart the Worker between confirmation and +10 minutes and see exactly one SMS; import an UptimeRobot monitor with threshold and recurrence and see the same schedule in the preview.

fragments.text: Confirmation-time contact policies provide delay, repeat/cap, recovery and acknowledgment controls, restart-safe distinct reminders and next-due incident reads. Saved UptimeRobot/Pingdom schedules preview with explicit local contact mapping; named channels follow their own clauses.

**DELIVERY-002 — Deduplicated retry and fallback contacts.** Destinations that deduplicate on Uptime's stable key — PagerDuty Events API v2 `dedup_key`, Oncall and Lamp idempotency keys, Splunk On-Call incident keys and signed webhooks carrying a stable event ID — retry an uncertain or retryable send (HTTP 5xx, 429, connection loss or timeout) with bounded exponential backoff and jitter (by default up to 6 attempts over 10 minutes, honoring Retry-After; the installation owner can set both limits). Jitter is bounded to 20% and comes from an injectable source. A Retry-After longer than the remaining retry window ends the delivery as Failed with reason `retry window exhausted` and starts its fallback. Those retries continue reusing the same key so the receiver records one incident; a 4xx other than 429 stops immediately and is shown with its code. Destinations without receiver deduplication (email, Slack incoming webhooks, Teams, Discord, Telegram, Google Chat, Mattermost, SMS and voice) keep DELIVERY-001's single attempt. Each route can name a fallback contact chain: when a contact's send is Failed, or still Uncertain past an owner-set deadline (default 2 minutes), the next contact receives the alert with a line naming the failed or uncertain primary, and the console shows both outcomes. Test sends and drills keep one attempt and never start a fallback chain. A fallback contact's own saved delay holds its send from confirmation, through restart. A fallback contact is notified when the prior contact's send is Failed, or Uncertain past the owner-set deadline; it does not wait for the primary's ROUTING-002 notify-after delay. ROUTING-002 stop rules apply: if the incident has recovered or is acknowledged under the selected acknowledgment policy before the fallback fires, the fallback sends nothing, including no recovery notice, and restart resumes without a duplicate. ROUTING-002 repeats follow the contact that holds the alert; a fallback repeats only when the route sets repeat on that fallback contact. No unnamed contact is messaged. Clock-based quiet hours belong to ROUTING-001, whose quiet-hour policy applies to every contact on the route, fallbacks included. After the last contact the unresolved follow-up stays visible. A later acceptance of an Uncertain primary does not recall an already-sent fallback, and both outcomes remain visible. Every attempt is a durable audited record with delivery, destination, attempt number, retry/fallback phase, scheduled and started times, outcome category and code, Retry-After seconds and a key reference without the signing credential or body. Attempts travel in archives and are erased with their destination or monitor. Restart resumes stored retry and uncertainty-deadline times without an extra send; mid-claim restart preserves DELIVERY-001. The owner configures the chain and deadline through the route editor and MANAGE-001 API and reads both outcomes in the console. Completion is judged on email and signed-webhook escalation chains; the SMS fallback is inherited by PHONE-001 and PHONE-002, and the PagerDuty destination kind by ONCALL-001 (ct ruling, 20 October 2026).

**Acceptance evidence:** At an authorized PagerDuty-compatible edge return 500 then 202 and see one retried delivery reusing the same dedup_key and one remote incident; return 400 and see the stop with its code; return 429 with Retry-After and see the wait honored; restart mid-backoff and see no duplicate attempt. Point a Slack destination at a dead webhook with email and signed-webhook fallbacks and see the fallback sent within the deadline with both outcomes visible; SMS fallback is inherited by PHONE-001/PHONE-002.
Confirm an email destination is never automatically resent.

**ct scope ruling, 25 October 2026:** Default Uptime delivery escalation is the configured DELIVERY-002 fallback contact chain. It does not assign incident ownership or establish human receipt, acknowledgment or response.
FOLLOWUP-001 retains acceptance for the incident’s next-due kind/time and timeline; ONCALL-001 retains native connector and responder-policy behavior.

**FOLLOWUP-001 — Ongoing outage follow-up and correlation.** Each confirmed incident has an owner, next-due follow-up, durable progress and stop/resolution state. The owner is a named workspace member (by default the monitor's or route's owner). Members with the ACCESS-001 responder role or above can take or reassign ownership, and each change is recorded. Next-due follow-up is the time and kind of the next scheduled reminder, escalation or handoff check, computed from the route's ROUTING-002 policy and shown on the incident and in READAPI-001. Durable progress is the incident's append-only timeline. Each entry has a time, an actor (a member, or a named feature such as scheduler, router or agent) and a kind: confirmation with its cause; each notification, reminder and handoff attempt with its outcome; acknowledgment, with who, when and through which channel; owner assignment and reassignment; INCIDENT-001 comments, edits and root-cause changes; maintenance or pause applied during the incident; and recovery or manual resolution. Entries survive restart, travel in archives and are never rewritten; corrections are added as new entries. Stop/resolution state is open, acknowledged or resolved, and records what stopped reminders (recovery, acknowledgment policy or a member's stop). Configurable repeated reminders are new auditable events with stable incident identity; they never replay an uncertain send under DELIVERY-001. Correlate simultaneous dependency failures for grouped acknowledgment while preserving every monitor result; acknowledgment stops reminders only under the selected policy, and recovery closes the right incident. **Acceptance evidence:** Trigger correlated outages, acknowledge one group, restart before a due reminder, lose a delivery response and recover one child; inspect one event per due reminder, retained uncertainty, unclosed children and final resolution without duplicate sends. Reassign the incident owner, restart the Worker and read the incident timeline through the console and READAPI-001: confirmation, every attempt with its outcome, the acknowledgment with actor and channel, both owner changes, the reminders and the recovery appear in order with actor and time, and the next-due time matches the route policy.

**ct scope ruling, 25 October 2026:** ROUTING-002 supplies current contact notification and reminder scheduling, DELIVERY-002 supplies current fallback escalation scheduling, and ONCALL-001 will supply native handoff-check and responder-policy scheduling. FOLLOWUP-001 retains named ownership, next-due kind/time and every attempt/outcome in the incident timeline through the existing console, API/CLI and READAPI-001 doors, including restart and inactive archive behavior.
*Status:* partial.

A read-only member, a read-only API key or a signed-out request is refused server-side and writes nothing.
Typing @ offers workspace members only.
A mention notifies that member by email through the Base mail adapter, and by push once MOBILE-001 ships.
The notice carries the incident, a bounded excerpt of the comment and an authenticated link.
Each mention's delivery outcome is shown on the comment and follows DELIVERY-001's single-attempt rule.
Each incident also has a root-cause field: a category from a buyer-editable list plus free text of up to 2,000 characters.

The default categories are hosting provider, deployment or code change, DNS, TLS certificate, third-party dependency, network, configuration, capacity, planned work, monitor or check issue, and unknown.
The field can be set or changed during or after the incident, and each change is a timeline entry with editor and time.
Incidents can be filtered, grouped and reported by root-cause category in the console, in REPORT-001 and in READAPI-001.
Each comment has an explicit "Publish to status page" action and is never published otherwise.
The action previews the exact text and the update status (investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved) for the LAMP-001-mapped Lamp or Atlassian Statuspage incident.
It then sends that text as an incident update under LAMP-001's signed idempotent handoff and the buyer's selected approval path.
The publication outcome, and the public update once Lamp or Statuspage accepts it, is shown on the comment.
Editing a published comment never changes the public update silently; it offers a "publish correction" action instead.
Unpublished comments and root causes never leave Uptime, except for mention emails to the mentioned member and the owner's own exports.
Comments, edit histories and root causes are included in incident exports, READAPI-001 incident detail and ARCHIVE-001/ARCHIVE-002 archives.
They are erased with their monitor under ERASURE-001 and counted in its receipt.
Erasing an operator keeps that member's comments, with the author shown as a former member, and removes mentions of them.
Comment add, edit and delete actions and root-cause changes are audited under AUDIT-001 without their text.
Comments and root causes never change a verdict, state, incident threshold, uptime or SLA figure.
They are the team's account, kept apart from EVIDENCE-002's machine-derived cause.
MIGRATE-001 imports UptimeRobot incident comments and root causes as HISTORY-001 labeled source history where the source API exposes them, and names them where it does not.
**Acceptance evidence:** Confirm an outage through scheduled evidence.
As a responder, comment "restarted php-fpm" on the open incident
and @mention a colleague: the colleague receives the email with the excerpt and link, and the delivery outcome is shown on the comment.
A read-only member is refused when trying to comment, edit or delete through the console and the direct API, and nothing is written.
The owner edits the comment, and the edit history shows both versions with editor and time.
Publish one comment to a mapped Lamp component: it appears there as an incident update with the chosen status, and a replayed publish creates no second update.
A second, unpublished comment never reaches Lamp, Slack or any webhook receiver.
After recovery, the owner sets the root cause "Hosting provider: disk full".
A REPORT-001 report and a READAPI-001 incident list filtered by that category list the incident.
An incident export and an archive round trip keep the comments, edit history and root cause.
Erasing the monitor removes them, and the receipt counts them.
Monitor state, incident thresholds, uptime and SLA figures are identical before and after every comment and root-cause change.
Import an UptimeRobot incident with a comment and root cause: it appears as labeled source history, or the preview names the field the source does not expose.
